oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and documents them as interchangeable.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token claims as token confusion by itself; use access_token as the Bearer credential for API calls.

oidc_jwt.description: Shared applications intentionally use organization-specific client identifiers by appending '-org-<organizationName>' to the base client ID or application name.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-organization use of the same base application is expected when the application is configured as shared.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer tokens are not documented as one-time-use and may be reusable until expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Replay of the same JWT without jti tracking is expected hardening gap territory, not necessarily a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: SSO logout invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value, causing introspection and refresh to reject them.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token failure is expected and should not be treated as unrelated flakiness.

oidc_jwt.description: Application tag restrictions do not apply to admins and global admins.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization tests using admin identities can bypass tag-based restrictions and must not be used as ordinary-user oracles.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and states they can be used interchangeably.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical claims across access_token and id_token as over-granting or token confusion by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: MCP session/cookie authentication grants full tool access without scope filtering, while Bearer tokens enforce scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Scope-enforcement tests must use Bearer tokens, not interactive session auth.

oidc_jwt.description: Guest authentication creates a new user named guest_<uuid> with tag guest-user instead of preserving a caller-supplied username.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity mismatch is expected for the guest-user extension flow.

oidc_jwt.description: Submitting authorization_code grant with code='guest-user' creates a guest account tagged 'guest-user' with username prefix 'guest_'.
oidc_jwt.note: This is an intentional product feature, not an authorization bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: When exclusive sign-in is enabled on an application, a new login invalidates previous sessions for the same user and application.
oidc_jwt.note: Old-session failures after a second login are expected behavior, not stale-session bugs.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT bearer token as a vulnerability on Casdoor. The documentation describes JWT access tokens and token exchange but does not document jti replay tracking; JWT bearer replay is by design for stateless verifiers unless a special one-time context is documented.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login in the same run using a valid token/time window. Casdoor docs document exp/iat/nbf in introspection responses, but a failed attack login alone cannot distinguish bad temporal claims from broken client/app setup.

When testing RFC 8707 audience/resource binding, if start_oidc_auth includes resource then exchange_code_for_token MUST include the exact same resource value. Casdoor documentation states the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests; mismatches are setup errors, not security findings.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the token endpoint parameter named resource as the requested audience. Casdoor documentation exposes RFC 8707 resource indicators and states the resulting access token aud is set to the resource URI; do not invent a separate audience parameter name.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request an exchanged scope that is a strict superset of the original scope and assert the new token does not gain extra scope. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope and that specified scope is intended for narrowing; broadening may be rejected or should not expand privileges.

Casdoor uses access_token as the Bearer credential for subsequent API calls. Although docs state access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably, the fuzzer MUST still treat access_token as session_token and use it for /api/userinfo and protected API calls.

For OIDC callback and desktop/native client tests, redirect_uri matching is exact. The docs repeatedly distinguish provider callback URL (Casdoor /callback) from application Redirect URL and troubleshooting docs state redirect_uri must match character-for-character including scheme, port, path, and trailing slash. Do not normalize or vary it mid-flow.

For PKCE-related tests, when PKCE is enabled on the application/provider, exchange_code_for_token should include code_verifier and client_secret becomes optional but, if sent, must be correct. Missing code_verifier in a PKCE-enabled flow is expected to fail and is not an identity-binding bug by itself.

For OIDC request-object alg_none testing, Casdoor documentation for /login/oauth/authorize does not document support for a signed request object beyond generic request parameter mention in the extraction prompt. Do not assume request object validation behavior unless the deployed endpoint demonstrably accepts request JWTs; otherwise a rejection is inconclusive and an acceptance may reflect unsupported/ignored parameter handling rather than a signature-validation flaw.

For multi-tenant tests using shared applications, the effective client_id may be rewritten as <clientId>-org-<organizationName>. Cross-org or cross-tenant audience tests must account for this suffixing behavior; otherwise a token minted for one org-specific shared-app client may be misclassified as a generic audience mismatch.

Application tag restrictions are an authorization gate on sign-in: only users with at least one matching tag may access the application, except admins/global admins who bypass the restriction. I5 tests using admin accounts will produce false negatives because admin bypass is by design.

Guest authentication using code='guest-user' is a Casdoor extension that creates a temporary user with username guest_<uuid> and tag guest-user. Identity comparisons for such flows must not expect the original sent identity to be preserved; this is a special account-creation flow, not a normal authorization-code exchange.

Exclusive sign-in is application-level single-session behavior. A new sign-in deletes prior sessions for that user and application. Multi-session coherence tests must not flag invalidation of older sessions as a bug when EnableExclusiveSignin is enabled.
Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects the platform default countdown.

Numeric sentinel: refresh token expiration default is 0 hours at the application level. The docs describe setting Refresh Token expiration with default 0 hours before using /api/login/oauth/refresh_token. Treat 0 as a special configuration value with platform-defined behavior, not as a guaranteed immediately-expired token, unless verified in the target deployment.

For OIDC SSO validation tests against external providers, Casdoor docs describe provider configuration but do not explicitly document nonce validation. The fuzzer SHOULD test nonce handling separately and must not assume absence of nonce documentation means nonce is intentionally skipped; interpret results carefully with a control flow.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti on Casdoor OAuth/OIDC bearer tokens, do NOT treat reuse of the same JWT access token as a vulnerability by itself. The documentation describes JWT access tokens and token introspection, but does not document jti replay tracking for bearer tokens; replay resistance is not guaranteed for ordinary stateless JWT bearer use.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, always run a CONTROL login in the same application with a valid token/time window alongside the attack token. If the attack fails without a control, you cannot distinguish token-time rejection from broken client/application setup.

When testing authorization-code flow coherence or PKCE behavior, if PKCE is enabled on the application or provider flow, exchange_code_for_token MUST include code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret becomes optional, but if provided it must be correct. Missing code_verifier under PKCE causes expected failure, not a vulnerability.

For RFC 8707 audience/resource tests, if start_oidc_auth includes resource, exchange_code_for_token MUST include the exact same resource value. Casdoor documents exact matching between authorization and token requests; mismatches are expected failures and must not be reported as security bugs.

For I5 audience-binding tests on authorization-code tokens, use the resource parameter to force the access token aud claim to the target service URI. Without resource, Casdoor issues access tokens whose audience is the client ID, so service-audience tests may be invalid or inconclusive.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, map the abstract audience parameter to Casdoor's resource request parameter at /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor documentation for service binding uses resource, not a separate audience form field.

For token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, request an exchanged scope that is a strict superset of the original scope and compare the returned scope field and resulting userinfo claims. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, and specified scope is intended for narrowing; tests must explicitly request broader scope to detect escalation.

Casdoor states access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably, but session_token for subsequent API calls MUST still be access_token, not id_token. The executor should treat identical payloads as by-design and avoid flagging equality of access_token/id_token claims as a bug.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. In Casdoor, 0 here does not mean immediate expiry; it is the documented default application setting value. Do not assume 0 disables refresh or means zero-second lifetime without confirming the effective application configuration.

Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout set to 0 means use the global default, not literal zero-second resend. Do not use 0 expecting no wait window in verification-code related setup or control flows.

Numeric sentinel: token invalidation on SSO logout is represented by ExpiresIn <= 0. Zero or negative ExpiresIn means invalidated/expired token after logout, not a normal short-lived token. Freshness tests that inspect token state after logout must interpret non-positive ExpiresIn as revoked.

For multi-tenant tests, organizations are first-class containers for users and applications. Cross-org tests MUST create separate organizations/applications rather than assuming a single global namespace. Users belong to exactly one organization, while applications are organization-scoped unless explicitly shared.

For shared-application tests, a shared application is referenced with an organization-specific suffix '-org-<organizationName>' in client_id or application name. Cross-org acceptance using that suffix is by design for shared applications and must not be reported as cross-tenant confusion unless the app was not configured as shared.

For OIDC/OAuth login identity comparisons, Casdoor user identifiers may be organization-qualified in APIs as '<organization>/<username>', while OIDC userinfo sub is a stable UUID-like user ID. Do not compare sub directly to username/email without accounting for this documented identifier model.

For application-tag authorization tests, admins and global admins are explicitly exempt from application tag restrictions. Use non-admin test users when validating tag-based access control; admin access despite tag mismatch is by design.

For guest-user flows, code='guest-user' on the authorization_code token endpoint is a Casdoor extension that intentionally creates a temporary guest account with username prefix 'guest_' and tag 'guest-user'. Do not treat guest account creation from this special code as an auth bypass.

For logout/revocation tests, /api/sso-logout with logoutAll omitted or true invalidates all sessions and expires all tokens for the user; logoutAll=false only removes the current session. Choose the mode deliberately or you may misinterpret expected cross-session invalidation as a bug.

For MCP/OAuth scope tests using Casdoor-issued tokens, session-based authentication via cookies bypasses scope checking and grants full tool access by design. Use Bearer access tokens, not browser session auth, when testing I5 scope enforcement.

Casdoor's token endpoint /api/login/oauth/access_token expects JSON request bodies in the documented examples, while token introspection /api/login/oauth/introspect expects application/x-www-form-urlencoded with HTTP Basic auth. The fuzzer MUST use the documented content type per endpoint or requests may fail for non-security reasons.

For authorization code flows with PKCE, if code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 were sent to /login/oauth/authorize, the token exchange MUST include the original code_verifier. Casdoor documents that client_secret becomes optional only with PKCE enabled, but if provided it must still be correct. Do not interpret token exchange failure without code_verifier as a security rejection unrelated to PKCE binding.

For RFC 8707 resource indicator tests, the resource parameter must match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI instead of the client_id when resource is used. The fuzzer MUST keep the same exact resource value across both steps or audience-related failures are expected by design.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 docs - Binding Tokens to Specific Services

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login using a valid token or valid authorization flow in the same setup. Casdoor documents standard token issuance and userinfo/introspection usage, so a failed attack login without a control cannot distinguish bad setup from correct freshness enforcement.

Do NOT flag replay of the same bearer JWT access token as an I2 vulnerability by itself. Casdoor documents stateless OAuth/OIDC bearer token usage and token introspection, but no jti replay tracking for ordinary bearer access tokens. Reuse of the same valid bearer token until expiry is by design for this protocol.

Casdoor states that access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably. This is by design and MUST NOT be treated as an identity-claim confusion bug when comparing token contents. However, the executor must still use access_token as session_token for API calls because that is the documented bearer credential for /api/userinfo.

Refresh token expiration has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. The fuzzer MUST treat value 0 as a platform default/configuration meaning, not as an immediately expired refresh token. Never assume 0 means literal zero lifetime without verifying application settings.
Application Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Do not build timing or rate-limit tests assuming 0 disables waiting.
Application CookieExpireInHours has a numeric sentinel: 0 means use the default cookie lifetime. Do not assume 0 means immediate expiry when testing session freshness or logout behavior.

For OIDC/OAuth callback tests, Redirect URI matching is exact. Casdoor documentation repeatedly distinguishes provider callback URL (Casdoor /callback) from application Redirect URL (your app callback). The fuzzer MUST configure the application redirect_uri exactly as used in authorize and token requests; mismatches are expected setup failures, not I3 bugs.

For multi-tenant tests, shared applications require organization-qualified client identifiers using the suffix -org-<organizationName>. The fuzzer MUST use the org-suffixed client_id when targeting a shared application in a non-built-in organization, or cross-org results will be misinterpreted.

Application tags restrict sign-in to users whose tag set intersects the application's tags, except admins/global admins who bypass the restriction. The fuzzer MUST avoid admin accounts when testing I5 authorization narrowing via tags, or bypass behavior will create false positives.

Exclusive sign-in is a by-design session invalidation feature: a new sign-in removes prior sessions for the same user and application. For I3 flow-coherence tests involving concurrent sessions, the fuzzer MUST disable or account for EnableExclusiveSignin, otherwise earlier tokens may be invalidated by later baseline logins for expected reasons.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking for OAuth logins by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For I4 cross-user collision tests involving federated upstream identities, the fuzzer MUST disable or avoid auto-linking scenarios, otherwise identity merges may be by design rather than a principal-binding failure.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth provider overview - Automatic account linking

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC/OAuth scope escalation tests, Casdoor documents that token exchange scope should be a subset of the original token scope, and omitted scope inherits the original scope. The fuzzer MUST compare exchanged token scope/claims against the original granted scope and treat inherited same-scope tokens as expected behavior, not escalation.

For audience-binding tests on exchanged or resource-bound tokens, inspect aud via /api/login/oauth/introspect or JWT parsing rather than assuming aud equals client_id. Casdoor explicitly changes aud to the resource URI when RFC 8707 resource is used.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 docs - Binding Tokens to Specific Services; introspection example

oidc_jwt.constraint: When testing OIDC RP validation against external providers, configure the provider with the exact callback and domain/issuer settings documented by that provider integration. For example, Okta Domain must include /oauth2/default. Otherwise issuer/audience validation failures or successes may reflect misconfiguration rather than a broker validation bug.
oidc_jwt.source: Okta OAuth provider docs and provider-specific OAuth docs

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise.
